input_shape_note: Height and width are DYNAMIC -- pass the image at its native resolution, do NOT resize it yourself. Resize (224x224, bilinear, antialias) and channel normalization happen INSIDE the ONNX graph (opset 18 Resize op with antialias=1), not in JS.
why_resize_is_in_the_graph: Measured empirically (headless Chromium + Playwright against the golden vectors below) that browser canvas resize -- both plain drawImage and createImageBitmap(resizeQuality:'high') -- could NOT reproduce the training pipeline's PIL/torchvision antialiased bilinear resize closely enough: max abs logit diff up to 0.34 on organs needing real downsampling (breast/lung), vs. colon (source already 224x224, no resize needed) which matched to ~1e-6. Baking the resize into the ONNX graph means the identical ONNX Runtime Resize op runs on both the training machine and in the browser -- one implementation, not two being reconciled after the fact.
client_side_steps: Decode the uploaded image (any resolution, JPEG/PNG).
Convert to RGB, drop any alpha channel.
Rearrange from HWC to NCHW -- shape [1, 3, H, W].
Do NOT resize. Do NOT normalize (subtract mean / divide std) -- the graph does both.

size_safety_cap.note: Purely a memory/perf safety valve for unusually large uploads (e.g. a phone photo), not a precision requirement -- none of the training datasets or golden vector images exceed ~800px. If you must pre-downscale an oversized upload before feeding the graph, do it to well above 2000px->224px isn't needed; downscaling only large outliers to ~2000px on the long side keeps the graph's own antialiased resize doing the precision-critical work.

rescale_note: divide raw 0-255 pixel values by 255 to get 0-1 range -- this is the ONLY numeric transform the client applies
mean_std_note: Informational only -- already baked into the ONNX graph, applied after the internal resize. Not ImageNet stats; computed from this project's own training split. You do not need to apply these yourself.
output_note: Model always returns all 3 output tensors regardless of selected organ. Use the case's declared organ to pick which tensor to read; ignore the other two. Apply softmax over each tensor's 2 values to get probabilities; argmax picks the class.
